# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 1
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 1

---

*[The apostles divide the world. Thomas receives India. He is sold as a slave.]*

1. At that time we the apostles were all in Jerusalem — Simon Peter and Andrew his brother, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax-collector, James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananean and Judas Iscariot — and we divided up the regions of the world, so that each of us should go into the region which fell to him by lot and the word he had heard.

2. By lot, India fell to Judas Thomas, who is also called Didymus [the Twin].

3. And he would not go, saying: "I do not have the strength to go, for I am weak in body. And how can I — a Hebrew man — go among the Indians and preach the truth?"

4. And while he was reasoning and saying this, the Lord appeared to him in a vision by night and said to him: "Fear not, Thomas; go to India and preach the word there, for my grace is with you."

5. But he would not obey, and said: "Send me wherever you wish, but to India I will not go."

6. And while he was reasoning thus, a certain merchant from India was there, one Abbanes by name, who had been sent by King Gundaphorus and had received orders from him to buy a skilled carpenter and bring him back.

7. And the Lord saw him in the market-place and said to him: "Do you wish to buy a carpenter?"

8. And he said: "Yes."

9. And the Lord said: "I have a slave who is a carpenter, and I wish to sell him." And he pointed out Thomas to him from afar.

10. And they agreed on a price of three litrae of uncoined silver, and they wrote a bill of sale. The writing of which was thus: "I, Jesus, the son of Joseph the carpenter, who dwells in Bethlehem of Judaea, declare that I have sold my slave Judas by name to you, Abbanes, a merchant of Gundaphorus, King of India."

11. And when the bill of sale was complete, the Lord took Judas Thomas and led him to Abbanes the merchant.

12. And when Abbanes saw him he said to him: "Is this your master?"

13. And the apostle answered and said: "Yes, he is my Lord."

14. And he said to him: "I have bought you from him." And the apostle held his peace.

---
*EMET note: Syriac preserves "Judas Thomas" — the full name. Greek recensions frequently use only "Thomas." "Didymus" (Greek "twin") interprets the Aramaic "Thomas/Toma." The bill of sale (v.10) in which Jesus signs himself "son of Joseph the carpenter" is one of the most remarkable passages in apocryphal literature.*
